title: Pullback compatibility of the hypercohomology-to-sheaf-cohomology edge
statement:
Let $(\mathcal C,\mathcal O)$ be a ringed site small in the common coefficient universe [def-weil-size-convention, def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology], with $\mathcal O$ a sheaf of commutative rings. Use module sheaves [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category], their unbounded derived category [def-weil-abstract-derived-category], cohomology sheaves $\mathcal H^n$ [def-weil-derived-cohomology-sheaves], and K-injective derived global sections $R\Gamma$ [def-pur-ringed-site-zeroth-hypercohomology]. Put $A=\Gamma(\mathcal C,\mathcal O)$. For $K\in D(\mathcal O)$ and $n\in\mathbf Z$, let $e_K^n:H^nR\Gamma(\mathcal C,K)\to\Gamma(\mathcal C,\mathcal H^nK)$ send a global cocycle in a K-injective representative to its class in the cohomology sheaf. Let $(\mathcal C',\mathcal O')$ be another such ringed site and let $g:(\operatorname{Sh}(\mathcal C'),\mathcal O')\to(\operatorname{Sh}(\mathcal C),\mathcal O)$ be a morphism of ringed topoi [def-weil-pbc-ringed-topos-morphism]. Use exact topos inverse image $g^{-1}$ and derived tensor pullback $Lg^*$ with its canonical adjunction [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-projection-mate-exact]. Define
$$r_{g,K}^n:g^*\mathcal H^nK=\mathcal O'\otimes_{g^{-1}\mathcal O}g^{-1}\mathcal H^nK\longrightarrow\mathcal H^n(Lg^*K)$$
by the tensor-of-cocycles pairing $\kappa^{0,n}$ of [def-sfb-ringed-site-module-cup-product], using $\mathcal H^0(\mathcal O'[0])=\mathcal O'$ and $\mathcal H^n(g^{-1}K)=g^{-1}\mathcal H^nK$. In local flat-term K-flat models it sends $b\otimes[z]$ to $[b\otimes z]$, with local lifts in a resolution of the scalar module when required. For $D\in D(\mathcal O')$ and $t:Lg^*K\to D$, define $P_{g,t}^n:H^nR\Gamma(\mathcal C,K)\to H^nR\Gamma(\mathcal C',D)$ by the derived adjunction unit $K\to Rg_*Lg^*K$, the canonical comparison $R\Gamma Rg_*\cong R\Gamma'$, and $R\Gamma'(t)$. Then, for $n\geq0$ and every $x$,
$$e_D^n(P_{g,t}^n(x))=\Gamma(\mathcal C',\mathcal H^n(t)\circ r_{g,K}^n)\bigl(g^*(e_K^n(x))\bigr).$$
Here $g^*$ on sections sends $s$ to $1\otimes g^{-1}s$. The maps $r_{g,K}^n$ and the displayed identity are natural in $K$ and $t$. No flatness of the structural ring map, exactness of tensor pullback, final site object, or boundedness is assumed; $r_{g,K}^n$ need not be invertible.

source.place: Tag 0BKV (lemma-sheafification-cohomology), naturality of the cocycle-to-sheaf map; derived-unit and global-sections normalization as in Tag 0D6H (lemma-Leray-unbounded). The nonflat tensor-pullback edge identity is agent-stated from these constructions.

proof.text: Put $U_n=\mathcal O_n$ and $U'_n=\mathcal O'_n$, with the structure sheaves in degree $n$. Apply [lem-sfb-ringed-hypercohomology-shifted-unit] to write $u=\gamma_K^n(x):U_n\to K$; then $e_K^n(x)=\mathcal H^n(u)(1)$. On the target use the same external ring $A=\Gamma(\mathcal C,\mathcal O)$, acting through $A\to\Gamma(\mathcal C',\mathcal O')$, so forgetting this action gives exactly the hypercohomology in the question. This does not change the edge map or its cocycle formula.

source.place: Tags 08JA (lemma-section-RHom-over-U), 0BKV (lemma-sheafification-cohomology), 07A6 (lemma-adjoint), 0D6H (lemma-Leray-unbounded), and 07A4 (lemma-pullback-tensor-product); shifted-unit argument for the nonflat edge identity.

proof.text: Write $L=Lg^*$, $R=Rg_*$ and $v=t\circ L(u):LU_n\to D$, identifying $LU_n\cong U'_n$ by the canonical unit and shift comparisons of [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-projection-mate-exact]. We claim $\gamma_D^n(P_{g,t}^n(x))=v$. Use the adjunction normalization in [lem-sfb-ringed-hypercohomology-shifted-unit] for the global-sections morphism $s$ and its composite $s g$. By [lem-sfb-ringed-derived-monoidal-comparisons], the Leray comparison is adjunction-compatible with that composite. Thus the image of $P_{g,t}^n(x)$ is the transpose, under $L\dashv R$, of $R(t)\eta_K u:U_n\to RD$. Naturality of the unit gives $R(t)\eta_K u=R(tL(u))\eta_{U_n}=R(v)\eta_{U_n}$. Its transpose is $\varepsilon_D L(R(v)\eta_{U_n})=v\varepsilon_{LU_n}L\eta_{U_n}=v$, by counit naturality and the adjunction triangle. This proves the claim with the specified Leray comparison.

source.place: Tags 08JA (lemma-section-RHom-over-U), 0BKV (lemma-sheafification-cohomology), 07A6 (lemma-adjoint), 0D6H (lemma-Leray-unbounded), and 07A4 (lemma-pullback-tensor-product); shifted-unit argument for the nonflat edge identity.

proof.text:
The tensor-of-cocycles pairing in [def-sfb-ringed-site-module-cup-product] is natural in the second argument: applying a cochain map to a local cocycle before tensoring gives the same tensor as applying its tensor-induced map afterwards; coboundaries map to coboundaries. Its canonical resolution identifications make this also an equality for derived morphisms. Apply it to $g^{-1}u:g^{-1}U_n\to g^{-1}K$. The exact inverse image and the definition of $r$ give
$$\mathcal H^n(Lu)\,r_{g,U_n}^n=r_{g,K}^n\,g^*\mathcal H^n(u).$$
The complex $U_n$ has one flat term. Under the unit and shift comparisons, $r_{g,U_n}^n$ is the identity on $\mathcal O'$: the pairing of the unit class with a scalar class is $b\otimes a\mapsto ba$. Thus
$$\mathcal H^n(Lu)(1)=r_{g,K}^n(1\otimes g^{-1}(\mathcal H^n(u)(1))).$$
This calculation uses only the flat shifted unit, and makes no flatness claim about $K$ or the structural ring map.

source.place: Tags 08JA (lemma-section-RHom-over-U), 0BKV (lemma-sheafification-cohomology), 07A6 (lemma-adjoint), 0D6H (lemma-Leray-unbounded), and 07A4 (lemma-pullback-tensor-product); shifted-unit argument for the nonflat edge identity.

proof.text:
Apply the edge evaluation of [lem-sfb-ringed-hypercohomology-shifted-unit] to the morphism $v$ found in step 2. Steps 1 and 3 yield
$$e_D^n(P_{g,t}^n(x))=\mathcal H^n(t)\mathcal H^n(Lu)(1)=\mathcal H^n(t)r_{g,K}^n(1\otimes g^{-1}e_K^n(x)),$$
which is the asserted identity of global sections. For a derived map $f:K\to K_1$, naturality of the pairing in step 3 gives $\mathcal H^n(Lf)r_{g,K}^n=r_{g,K_1}^n g^*\mathcal H^n(f)$. Naturality of $\gamma$ and of the adjunction unit gives the corresponding naturality of $P$; postcomposition $t\mapsto a\circ t$ is functoriality of $R\Gamma'$ and $\mathcal H^n$. Hence both $r$ and the equality have the required naturality. The proof works for every integer $n$, in particular for $n\geq0$.
